definitions.note: adjective defining a noun: the answer is the reactive after-effect of something

parts.note: dorsal means of the back
ablutions are a wash, a cleansing of the body

explanation.surface: Someone washing their back in an anxious, reactive mood.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose in part of speech: the answer names a reaction or after-effect rather than describing one.
explanation.definitionFit: A backwash is the repercussion or reaction that follows an event, as water surges back after a wave.

parts.note: take the forty-thieves hero's name and drop his first name, and you are left with a rum-soaked cake

explanation.walkthrough: Ali Baba without 'Ali' leaves the cake name; a rum baba is a yeast cake soaked in rum syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum baba is a small sponge cake steeped in rum, so the leftover surname names something rum-flavoured.

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Reactively by the means of' and the scan line is illegible ('Reactively c..ments (5-4)'?), so no definition or wordplay can be read for the answer

parts.note: a castrated ram hung with a bell leads the flock, giving the word for a leader of a movement

explanation.walkthrough: A bellwether is the belled ram that leads the sheep; put a bell on this animal and you have a ringleader.
explanation.definitionFit: A wether is a castrated ram, and the one wearing the bell leads the flock, hence a bellwether is a leader.

parts.note: quotes Keats's sonnet on Chapman's Homer, where Cortez's men look at each other 'with a wild ...' on a peak in Darien

explanation.walkthrough: Keats: 'Looked at each other with a wild surmise, Silent, upon a peak in Darien.'
explanation.definitionFit: A surmise is a guess or conjecture, the very word Keats used for the explorers' astonished speculation.

indicators.note: the two names are brought together and rearranged as one unit, so their letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Two friends, Ned and Mat, join forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teamed up' signals the anagram of NED and MAT, and the whole clue also describes the answer: two people working one behind the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Working in tandem means two people acting together, like riders on a two-seat bicycle.

parts.note: fill the gap in the title of Burns's song addressed to an old husband named John

explanation.walkthrough: The Burns song is 'John Anderson, my jo, John'; 'jo' is Scots for sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname completes the first line and title of the Burns poem about a long marriage.

indicators.note: a coiled snake is twisted round, so the letters of the word next to it are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Being afraid of a snake ready to strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coiled' rearranges ADDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear, and either word works as a verb meaning to be afraid of.

clue.text: Where the lemur feels most at home

definitions.text: Where the lemur feels most at home

parts.words: Where the lemur feels most at home
parts.note: lemurs live wild only on one large island off south-east Africa

explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are native only to Madagascar, the island off Africa's east coast.

clue.text: Get to work with the fastening

definitions.meaning: to ... to (or down) is to set to work in earnest
a clasp on a belt or strap

explanation.definitionFit: To buckle to is to apply yourself to a job, and a buckle is also the clasp that fastens a belt.

clue.text: Loud disapproval to a good man means the push

parts.note: a boo is a loud cry of disapproval
ST, for saint, is the crossword's good man

explanation.surface: A virtuous man is heckled, and that pushes him on.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost is a push upward or forward, a helpful shove.

clue.text: One treated in cavalier fashion by the opposition ?

definitions.text: One treated in cavalier fashion by the opposition ?

parts.words: One treated in cavalier fashion by the opposition ?
parts.note: in the English Civil War the king's men were Cavaliers, and their opponents, Parliament's supporters, were the crop-haired party

explanation.walkthrough: 'cavalier' looks like an adjective meaning offhand; it points to the Cavaliers, Royalists who fought Parliament's soldiers in the English Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Roundheads were the Parliamentarians of the English Civil War, opponents of the Royalist Cavaliers.

parts.note: a star-shaped mark used in typesetting, from the Greek for little star

explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the small printed star symbol used to mark a footnote.

clue.text: How to make a ridge, at the second attempt

definitions.text: How to make a ridge, at the second attempt

parts.words: How to make a ridge, at the second attempt
parts.note: to throw up a mound of earth a second time you would turn the soil over once more with a spade

explanation.walkthrough: Digging again throws up a fresh ridge of soil; the letters of the answer also rearrange to RIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To redig is to dig over again, which piles up soil a second time.

parts.note: 'song and dance' sounds like a fuss, but the answer is literally both: a French Revolutionary song that was also danced in the streets

explanation.walkthrough: 'A song and dance' is British for a needless fuss; here it is meant literally. The carmagnole was a song and round dance of the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The carmagnole was a revolutionary French song with an accompanying street dance.

indicators.note: what is heard is a spoken phrase, so the phrase for a young woman is taken by its sound

parts.note: a damsel is a lass, so 'a damsel' is a lass

explanation.surface: A damsel in distress, crying out to be rescued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' says that 'a lass' sounds like the cry of distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an exclamation of grief or dismay, what someone in distress cries out.

clue.text: "The main opinion he held once Of fantasy, of dreams, and " (J. Caesar)

definitions.text: "The main opinion he held once Of fantasy, of dreams, and " (J. Caesar)

parts.words: "The main opinion he held once Of fantasy, of dreams, and " (J. Caesar)
parts.note: fill the gap in Cassius's line in Julius Caesar about how Caesar has grown superstitious

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare: 'Quite from the main opinion he held once Of fantasy, of dreams, and ceremonies.' Here the word means omens or portents.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare uses the plural for omens and portents, the rites and signs Caesar once scorned.

parts.note: the same short word is a student prank or festival of fun and also an old, shabby piece of clothing

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a rag is a student charity carnival full of pranks; glad rags are clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A rag is both student horseplay (rag week) and a scrappy garment, as in glad rags.

parts.note: Pierre Loti's novel Pêcheur d'Islande follows a Breton who fishes in far northern waters

explanation.walkthrough: Pierre Loti's 1886 novel is known in English as An Iceland Fisherman.
explanation.definitionFit: Loti's fisherman sails to the cod banks off Iceland, so he is Icelandic in the sense of belonging to those seas.

parts.note: Wagner's knight arrives and leaves in a boat drawn by a white bird, so his final song suits that bird

explanation.walkthrough: Lohengrin is the swan knight of Wagner's opera; a farewell performance is a swan song.
explanation.definitionFit: A swan song is a final performance, and Lohengrin's swan makes it literal.

parts.note: a dieter dreads anything that tips the scales upward, and a small extra thrown in to reach a weight is a trifle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' suggests the creamy pudding a dieter avoids; it means something of little worth added to make up a weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A makeweight is a minor item added to make up a weight, so a trifle; a slimmer hates gaining weight.

parts.note: a cold store that hands out chilled food, described as if it were a cold person

explanation.definitionFit: An icebox is a refrigerator, a cold cabinet from which food is taken.

parts.note: the gods in the Iliad and Odyssey roar with unquenchable mirth, giving a phrase for vast laughter

explanation.definitionFit: Homeric laughter is loud, irrepressible laughter like that of the gods in the Greek epics.

clue.text: Divine model for a male artist

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A goddess sits for a portrait by a male painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hera, queen of the Olympian gods, is a divine figure and a model of the wife.

definitions.meaning: the old word for a standard-bearer, as Iago is Othello's 'ancient'
a man who carries the regiment's colours, its flag

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient' is not old here: it is a corruption of this very rank, used by Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank of standard-bearer was once spelt 'ancient', and the officer carried the regimental colours.

clue.text: Proceed to: the front from Lanarkshire

definitions.note: defines a place: a town lying in the Scottish county

parts.note: to go is to proceed
the van is the front of an army, as in vanguard

explanation.surface: Instructions to head for the front line, issued from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: Govan is a shipbuilding district on the Clyde, once a burgh of Lanarkshire, now part of Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: Govan, by the Clyde, was a burgh in the old county of Lanarkshire before joining Glasgow.

clue.text: What's it worth to be distinguished in farewell ?

indicators.note: the letter for distinguished is placed inside the word for farewell

parts.note: vale is Latin for goodbye
U means upper-class, socially distinguished

explanation.surface: Is a refined goodbye worth anything?
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British label for upper-class usage, hence distinguished.
explanation.definitionFit: Value is what a thing is worth, its price or merit.

clue.text: Lament perhaps about me? Cheese it !

indicators.note: the anagram goes around the word me
perhaps says the word lament is only one possible arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about themselves until told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns LAMENT into EMNTAL, and 'about' puts ME inside it. 'Cheese it' is old slang for stop it or run away.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a Swiss cheese with large holes.

clue.text: Scandinavian who gets the chopper at fifty !

parts.note: an axe is a chopper
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A Norseman faces the axe when he reaches fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Axel is a common Danish and Swedish man's name.

clue.text: Employed, of course, for the portrait of Mogul's chairman ?.

definitions.text: Employed, of course, for the portrait of Mogul's chairman ?.

parts.words: Employed, of course, for the portrait of Mogul's chairman ?.
parts.note: the head of an oil firm sitting for his portrait would naturally be painted in the medium made from his product

explanation.walkthrough: Mogul was a brand of motor oil, so its chairman is an oil man; portraits are traditionally painted in oils.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil colour is paint ground in oil, the classic medium for formal portraits.

clue.text: Some find exercises at the end of the book

definitions.text: at the end of the book

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following two words are taken, a run within them

explanation.surface: A textbook's practice exercises are printed at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run from 'find exercises'.
explanation.definitionFit: An index is the alphabetical list of topics found at the back of a book.

clue.text: Watts's physical display in Kensington Gardens

definitions.text: Watts's physical display in Kensington Gardens

parts.words: Watts's physical display in Kensington Gardens
parts.note: G. F. Watts's bronze horse and rider in the London park is titled Physical ...

explanation.walkthrough: The statue 'Physical Energy' by G. F. Watts stands in Kensington Gardens, a royal park in London. Watts is also the unit of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy completes the title of the Watts sculpture, and watts measure the rate energy is used.

clue.text: Like the view from some railways ?

definitions.text: Like the view from some railways ?

parts.words: Like the view from some railways ?
parts.note: a fairground switchback is called a scenic railway, and its view would be described with a related adjective

explanation.walkthrough: A scenic railway is an old name for a roller coaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenical is an old form of scenic, describing scenery or a fine view.
